title: Review of c11's active-nematic ringed rods (SIBMD): replicates on fresh seed 11; the surfactant ring sits right at the gate (rim/core 1.51 vs 0.93 with chis=0) and is passive
summary: Fresh seed 11 (128^2, T=1000) and the chis=0 twin on the same seed. From noise, droplets nucleate by t~85, become nematic rods that swim, elongate and pinch in two; the population grows from ~10 rods at t=135 to ~45 at t=1000. labkit: 21 persistent splits, max generation 3, merge/split 0.33, 45 tracks moved >= 1 body length (max 4.9). Four automatically found fissions (fission_strips_seed11.png) show three clean binary pinches of a rod into two rods, and one three-body tangle. Surfactant s: rim/core 1.51, rim/outside 2.17, 104/140 individuals membrane-like; with chis=0 the bodies and their divisions are identical (s does not act back) and s is a diffuse fill, rim/core 0.93, 0/140.

verdicts.limitation: The ring is exactly at the gate on this seed (aggregate rim/core 1.51) and does no work: s never acts back, so removing it changes nothing about motion or division. Motion is modest (max 4.9 body lengths, tracks broken by collisions), merge/split 0.33, and one of four sampled fissions is a multi-body tangle.
